justifications.functional_suitability: The system fully covers physical and digital cataloguing, circulation, and self-service via the Catalog & Circulation Controller, Catalog Module, Third-Party Digital Content Providers, and Patron Portal Component.
justifications.performance_efficiency: The sub-800ms search SLA (R-05) is addressed via a dedicated Search Engine (OpenSearch) with Query Execution & Scoring Engine, asynchronous index updates via Kafka and Index Synchronizer Component, and Read Replica Components.
justifications.compatibility: Explicit integration mechanisms are defined for external services, including Third-Party Identity Provider / LDAP via SAML/OIDC, Payment Gateway via REST, Digital Content Providers, and Notification Service using webhooks.
justifications.usability: All distinct user roles from the brief are addressed with dedicated frontend components: Patron Portal Component for patrons, Staff Circulation Dashboard Component for library staff, and Admin Analytics Dashboard Component for administrators.
justifications.reliability: Reliability is well supported by Resilience4j circuit breakers with database fallback in Catalog Search Component, Upstream Proxy & Circuit Breaker in API Gateway, and OpenSearch automated snapshots, though database disaster recovery specifics are light.
justifications.security: EU-only data residency is strictly constrained across storage nodes, CDN, and databases. Strong authentication via JWT/OAuth2 Validator, TLS 1.3 encryption, SASL/SCRAM, and Security & Audit Interceptor ensure complete security and GDPR compliance.
justifications.maintainability: The system exhibits clean separation of concerns across C4 levels, modular container isolation, and Schema Registry for contract evolution. However, the Core API Application still combines multiple domain responsibilities into single controllers/repositories.
justifications.portability: Containers use portable technologies like Spring Boot, React, and OpenSearch with clear boundary protocols (REST, AMQP/Kafka). Conformance to cloud-managed EU regions is clear, though infrastructure-as-code or specific multi-cloud adaptability is unmentioned.

PERF-01.justification: A dedicated OpenSearch cluster isolates full-text search and faceting from core transactional stores, backed by API gateway rate limiting and caching components, ensuring sub-800ms latency under high concurrent search traffic.
sensitivity_points: OpenSearch cluster sizing and shard distribution under peak concurrency
Connection pool throughput between Core API and Search Engine
tradeoffs: Resource costs of dedicated search clusters versus shared database query performance

PERF-02.justification: Catalogue modifications write to PostgreSQL and asynchronously publish events to Kafka. The Index Synchronizer in Async Workers updates OpenSearch decoupled from the read path, keeping P99 latency low while syncing items well within five minutes.
sensitivity_points: Kafka partition throughput and consumer processing lag in Async Workers
Search engine index refresh interval versus query latency impact
tradeoffs: Eventual consistency of catalog updates versus synchronous search index locking

AVAIL-01.justification: OpenSearch cluster coordination and multi-node storage handle node failover transparently. Furthermore, the Core API's Catalog Search Component includes Resilience4j circuit breaking with fallback to PostgreSQL read replicas, while loan transactions are completely isolated in the primary database.
sensitivity_points: Failover detection timeout in OpenSearch cluster coordination
Resilience4j circuit breaker trip threshold and replica query load
tradeoffs: Fallback to relational search risks degraded search features during cluster recovery

AVAIL-02.justification: The self-service frontend is a stateless SPA served via CDN, and backend API access routes through an API Gateway with upstream proxying and health checks. Loss of a frontend/client or gateway instance routes traffic seamlessly without affecting database transactions.
sensitivity_points: CDN failover speed and gateway upstream health check intervals
Client-side retry logic and state restoration via Shared API Client
tradeoffs: Stateless client architectures require robust token management and network re-try overhead

MOD-01.justification: The Payment & External Integration Service component encapsulates third-party digital content integrations. Adding a new e-book provider interacts through this service and standard ingestion pipelines, keeping modifications isolated from catalogue and circulation core logic.
sensitivity_points: Coupling between external provider schemas and internal ingestion models
tradeoffs: Adapter encapsulation overhead versus direct API integrations across modules

MOD-02.justification: While Library Administrators have configuration dashboards and circulation workflows are modeled, the architecture lacks an explicit business rules engine or dynamic configuration management system to modify differing institutional loan policies at runtime without code deployment.
sensitivity_points: Absence of runtime dynamic rule evaluation engine in the Core API
tradeoffs: Hardcoded domain rules simplify design but necessitate code changes across tenant types

SEC-01.justification: Data residency is enforced at every layer: EU-restricted CDN, managed PostgreSQL restricted to EU regions, OpenSearch cluster storage on EU cloud storage, and pseudonymized outbound connections to external systems ensure compliance by design.
sensitivity_points: Configuration of regional boundaries across all cloud storage and third-party gateways
tradeoffs: Restricting compute and storage exclusively to EU regions can limit provider redundancy options

SEC-02.justification: The API Gateway validates JWT/OAuth2 tokens and enforces ACLs, while the Core API Security & Audit Interceptor inspects authorization contexts to prevent unauthorized record access and emits immutable audit logs to the Centralized Log/Audit Aggregator.
sensitivity_points: Granularity of patron ownership checks inside the Security & Audit Interceptor
Tamper-proof streaming of security audit logs
tradeoffs: Synchronous authorization and interceptor audit overhead slightly increases request latency
